messages:
Alex K: Heads-up — customer reported SSE connections dropping ~90s after open. They get partial output then client immediately reconnects and sees duplicate chunks. Billing shows tokens counted twice.
Maria P: ugh. any request_id/idempotency token set by client?
Alex K: initial ticket says client doesn't set one. Using our hosted API with ALB in front.
Ingrid L: ALBs famously kill idle L7 conns if they see no bytes for X sec. TCP keepalive won't help at the ALB layer. We should use application-level pings/comments.
Ben S: confirm — if we send periodic SSE comment lines (":" or ": keepalive") it counts as activity and prevents ALB idle close.
SRE Oncall: +1. Also watch for proxies that terminate after the first 512B of no activity. Default ALB idle timeout is 60s, so 90s drop is plausible if client doesn't read/ack?
Maria P: customer says drop happens after ~90s consistently. Could be our internal proxy + external client idle. We should repro.
Alex K: repro steps I used: 
```
# reproduce with curl
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=gpt-x" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```
Let it sit until disconnect (~90s).

Server log snippet I captured: 
```
[2026-05-14T12:00:01Z] conn_id=abc123 opened
[2026-05-14T12:01:31Z] conn_id=abc123 read 0 bytes, closed by upstream (502)
```

Ingrid L: that log looks like the proxy closed for idle. Put a keepalive comment write every 15s and retry.
Ben S: simple Node handler suggestion: 
```
res.writeHead(200, {
  'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
  'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
  'Connection': 'keep-alive'
});
setInterval(() => res.write(': ping\n\n'), 15000);
```
This writes an SSE comment which is legal per spec and won't be treated as an event by clients.
Alex K: good. Also: client reconnect behavior — they currently reconnect immediately and re-request the same prompt which causes duplicate billing. We should recommend idempotency token.
Maria P: we already support `Idempotency-Key` header on generation endpoints. If client includes the same key we can dedupe billing and return previous stream. But client needs to provide it.
Ingrid L: for streaming resumes, support Last-Event-ID header to resume. If customer wants partial output resume we need to map event ids to prefix cache keys. Might be more work.
Ben S: short-term: add guidance in support runbook — 1) send SSE comment pings at 15s, 2) client should send Idempotency-Key on initial request, 3) client SDK: exponential backoff before reconnect (start 250ms -> 2s -> 5s) and avoid immediate duplicate requests.
SRE Oncall: I'll check ALB/proxy configs. If we increase ALB idle timeout we reduce risk, but default is safer for platform. App-level pings are the right default.
Alex K: action items:
- Alex K: create runbook doc + repro steps in ticket (this thread) — due EOD.
- Ingrid L: propose SSE ping interval and add sample code to SDK docs (15s default) — will PR tomorrow.
- Ben S: update client SDK reconnect logic to include Idempotency-Key header usage examples and backoff — will ship patch.
- SRE Oncall: capture packet-level trace for the impacted customer and confirm idle-close cause, see if any proxy-level 503/502 correlates.

Maria P: one billing note — we should detect quick reconnects with same source IP + same prompt and automatically pause double-charge while we verify idempotency. But that's tricky. For now note in runbook to check token and dedupe if present.
Alex K: agreed. Also added a sample curl with comment ping to the runbook.
SRE Oncall: posting ticket to follow-up: https://support.redwood.example/tickets/RI-5421 
Support Bot: Ticket RI-5421 created and linked to this thread.
Ben S: :thumbsup:
Ingrid L: @Alex K ping me once runbook draft is ready, I'll review. :eyes:
Alex K: will do — thanks everyone. :pray:
